changes.label: Section 3.7: add AI Testing and Observation
text: The supplementary AI assessment maps documented test results to four selected ISO/IEC 25059:2023 quality characteristics. Functional correctness is examined by checking whether replacement candidates satisfy the independently verified availability, schedule, shift, and post requirements. Robustness is examined through the workflow’s behavior when the AI service fails or the candidate information changes. Transparency is examined by checking whether the recommendation’s explanation agrees with the supplied records and whether AI advice can be distinguished from rule-based fallback. User controllability is examined by checking whether the administrator can confirm, reject, or change a recommendation before assignment.

For each assessed case, the researchers record the test condition, expected behavior, actual behavior, and supporting screenshot or log, together with the observer, test date, and system version. The record identifies whether the AI response was live, simulated, cached, or unavailable. Existing test records may be used when their conditions and outcomes can be traced. Where an observation is missing, the corresponding behavior is marked Not assessed until supporting evidence is recorded. The observation record is completed by the researchers and is not distributed as another questionnaire.

The findings are compared with the expected behavior and reported descriptively. A criterion is marked Met only when supported by the recorded observation, and Not met when the actual behavior differs from the expected result. These are study-specific reporting labels. Simulated AI failures support findings about validation and fallback behavior; they do not establish the quality of live model recommendations. The assessment covers the selected characteristics and observed scenarios rather than full conformity with ISO/IEC 25059.

The discussion identifies which quality characteristic is supported, the evidence used, and any limitation or observation still required. These findings are not combined with the questionnaire means, and no additional Likert rating or overall ISO/IEC 25059 score is calculated.

changes.label: Section 4.1: add Table 24A after Table 24 and its legend
text: AI Quality Assessment Based on ISO/IEC 25059:2023

The AI-assisted absence-handling feature was examined by mapping the existing test findings and documented behavior to selected ISO/IEC 25059:2023 quality characteristics. Table 24A identifies the available evidence and the limits of each interpretation. It uses the current paper’s reported results and does not treat an implemented feature as proof that every related quality requirement has been tested.

This supports continuity of the replacement workflow in those conditions. The documented screening and fallback results provide evidence for specific aspects of functional correctness and robustness within the tested workflow. Explanation accuracy and the administrator’s rejection, alternative-selection, and cancellation actions require separate observation records before a test finding can be reported. These observations can be collected during system testing without administering another questionnaire. The findings do not establish that AI ranking is superior to rule-based ranking or that the system conforms to all requirements of ISO/IEC 25059.

changes.label: Section 5.1: summarize the evidence and remaining observations
text: The supplementary ISO/IEC 25059 mapping identified reported evidence for candidate screening and preservation of the rule-based ranking during the tested AI failures. These findings support specific aspects of functional correctness and robustness. The paper describes explanatory reasoning and administrator confirmation, but separate observations are still needed to establish explanation accuracy and the outcomes of rejecting, changing, or cancelling a recommendation. These remaining checks are part of system testing rather than a new respondent evaluation.

changes.label: Section 5.2: align the AI conclusion with the available evidence
changes.before: Artificial intelligence is safest in this domain when it is placed where it can only improve an answer that already exists. Because the language model re-ranks a list the system’s own rules produced, the system continues to deliver qualified, ranked candidates when the model is unreachable, out of quota, disabled, or malformed in its reply. The study concludes that the advisory placement of AI defined in Chapter I is not a limitation accepted for safety’s sake alone, but the arrangement that makes the feature dependable for an agency whose stations must be covered whether or not an external service answers that afternoon.
changes.after: The advisory placement of AI allows the replacement workflow to retain its rule-based candidate ranking when the AI service cannot provide usable advice. The reported tests support this fallback behavior under the conditions examined. The ISO/IEC 25059 mapping therefore supports conclusions about the documented screening and fallback behavior, while further observations are needed for explanation accuracy and administrator control. The study does not establish that AI always improves the ranking or that the observed behaviors demonstrate full conformity with the standard.

changes.label: Section 5.3 recommendation 4: specify the remaining observations
changes.before: Analyze recorded administrator decisions against AI recommendations to measure usefulness and refine rule-based scoring weights. Maintain the golden-file contract test by running it before every release and documenting any endpoint differences in writing.
changes.after: Analyze recorded administrator decisions against AI recommendations to examine usefulness and refine rule-based scoring weights. Maintain the golden-file contract test by running it before every release and documenting endpoint differences. Complete the remaining ISO/IEC 25059 observations by comparing live explanations with the underlying records and recording the administrator’s rejection, alternative-selection, and cancellation actions. Retain the test conditions, actual outcomes, screenshots or logs, and system version as evidence, and repeat relevant checks after changes to the model, prompt, rules, or interface.
